commonly_attributed_claim: Searle argues that machines cannot think
what_the_paper_says: 'Only a machine could think, and indeed only very special kinds of machines' (p. 424); he rejects only the sufficiency of running a program (B 1)

commonly_attributed_claim: Searle rules out silicon minds
what_the_paper_says: 'I offer no a priori proof that a system of integrated circuit chips couldn't have intentionality. That is ... an empirical question' (p. 453) (B 1)

commonly_attributed_claim: Searle opposes artificial intelligence research
what_the_paper_says: 'I am all in favor of weak AI, at least as a research program' (p. 453); the target is strong AI's claim that the program is the explanation (B 1)

commonly_attributed_claim: Searle concedes nothing to the replacement arguments
what_the_paper_says: Author's Response: 'if the stimulation of the causes is at a low enough level to reproduce the causes ... the simulation will reproduce the effects' (pp. 452-453) (B notes 4)

commonly_attributed_claim: Dennett denies that conscious experience exists
what_the_paper_says: 'Since I don't deny the reality of conscious experience, I grant that conscious experience has properties'; what is denied is that any property is ineffable, intrinsic, private or directly apprehensible (G 1)

commonly_attributed_claim: Quining Qualia replies to the fading and dancing qualia arguments
what_the_paper_says: It predates Chalmers 1995 by seven years and does not cite him; the two meet at one premise about introspection, stated independently in the opposite time order (G 1)

commonly_attributed_claim: Quining Qualia answers the anti-functionalist literature generally
what_the_paper_says: Block's liberalism/chauvinism dilemma and the input-output problem are untouched, and Searle 1980 is not in the bibliography at all; the target is one premise family (G notes 5)

commonly_attributed_claim: Dennett concludes that a functional duplicate does have qualia
what_the_paper_says: He does not claim the wine-tasting machine has qualia; the conclusion withholds the affirmative verdict as much as the negative, and 'no qualia at all' is flagged as tactical (G 1, endnote 2)

commonly_attributed_claim: Dennett and the replacement arguments disagree about whether subjects are in error
what_the_paper_says: His conclusion is that there is no determinate fact; Cuda's step 2 and Chalmers's Joe are built against a systematic-error hypothesis. Whether they reach the no-fact case is addressed by no reviewed work (G notes 3)

commonly_attributed_claim: Aru et al. deny that machines could be conscious
what_the_paper_says: Three explicit disclaimers: not only mammalian brains, not only living systems, not impossible in software; the claim is about present systems and specificity (C 4)

commonly_attributed_claim: Piccinini is an anti-triviality theorist answering Putnam and Searle
what_the_paper_says: He calls their problem 'not very serious' (p. 281) because their mappings are anomalous, and raises a different surviving problem about bona fide descriptions (A2 notes 1)

commonly_attributed_claim: Blockhead is an argument against computational functionalism
what_the_paper_says: The list-searcher is offered against a reply to Block's own argument - 'this is just crude behaviorism' (pp. 281-282) - not against functionalism itself (A1 notes 5)

commonly_attributed_claim: Block refutes functionalism
what_the_paper_says: 'I do not claim that this is a conclusive argument against functionalism ... it is best construed as a burden-of-proof argument' (p. 296) (A1 3)

commonly_attributed_claim: Doerig et al.'s gloss: on IIT, recurrent systems are always conscious
what_the_paper_says: IIT requires a maximum of integrated information, not merely positive Phi (albantakis2023, p. 10); the unfolding construction respects maximality, so gloss and construction come apart (D notes 3)

commonly_attributed_claim: Chalmers established that the right computation is metaphysically sufficient for a mind
what_the_paper_says: A footnote added in 2011 restricts computational sufficiency and organizational invariance to nomological necessity, leaving zombies metaphysically possible (A2 5 s. 2.8)

commonly_attributed_claim: The fading and dancing qualia arguments prove that functional duplicates are conscious
what_the_paper_says: Section 5 states the conclusion is empirical (natural) impossibility only, and that the position is compatible with property dualism about experience (B 3)

commonly_attributed_claim: Cuda established that functional organisation suffices for consciousness
what_the_paper_says: He establishes sufficiency only at circuit functional equivalence and says so; what he claims more broadly is to disqualify material as a ground of objection (B 2)

commonly_attributed_claim: Block and Fodor concluded against a computational theory of mind
what_the_paper_says: 'It may be both true and important that organisms are probabilistic automata'; the target is the machine-table level, and computational states are offered as the repair (A1 1)

commonly_attributed_claim: Integrated information theory is carbon chauvinism
what_the_paper_says: Endnote 15: 'there is no reason why hardware-level, neuromorphic models ... could not approximate, one day, our level of consciousness' (D 1, D notes 7)

commonly_attributed_claim: Schwitzgebel and Garza run the Cuda-Chalmers replacement argument
what_the_paper_says: n. 5 (ms. p. 11): they assume consciousness is preserved and argue something ethical; Cuda and Chalmers try to establish the preservation (E 1 s. 2.3)

commonly_attributed_claim: Chalmers and Birch agree about language models, as their joint report shows
what_the_paper_says: They disagree: Birch says of a chatbot conversation that 'no one is there' (p. 13) while Chalmers holds a live credence; co-authorship is not corroboration (E notes 4-5)

commonly_attributed_claim: The report found no obvious barriers to building conscious AI systems
what_the_paper_says: A title-page footnote records that this sentence was revised: satisfying the indicators 'would not mean that such an AI system would definitely be conscious' (D 6)

commonly_attributed_claim: Sprevak cites Chalmers 1996 as the solution to universal realization
what_the_paper_says: He cites it to show how cheaply the counterfactual requirement is met given a clock and a dial (PDF p. 10 n. 9) - a reading of Chalmers's own concession (A2 notes 4)

commonly_attributed_claim: Fodor argued that the autonomous psychological level is computational
what_the_paper_says: He argues only that psychology does not reduce; the step from irreducible to computational is taken by others (A1 2)

commonly_attributed_claim: Seth refutes computational functionalism
what_the_paper_says: 'The arguments so far do not disprove computational functionalism. But they do render it less plausible, and less appealing' (section 3.6) (C 5)

commonly_attributed_claim: Consciousness Matters is an anti-functionalist paper
what_the_paper_says: It argues that consciousness has a function, and its anti-epiphenomenalism runs through multiple realizability (List's realization insensitivity) (C notes 2)

commonly_attributed_claim: Kleiner and Hoel restate the unfolding argument
what_the_paper_says: Self-described 'generalization and correction'; its second horn hits the functionalist theories that the unfolding argument exempts (D 5, D notes 5)

commonly_attributed_claim: The attention schema theory explains subjective experience
what_the_paper_says: 'The theory emphatically does not explain how we have a subjective experience. It explains how a machine claims to have a subjective experience' (p. 5) (D 3)

commonly_attributed_claim: Dehaene, Lau and Kouider answer the question of experience
what_the_paper_says: The experiential question is declared beyond scope (p. 492); what is offered instead is a covariation observation about blindsight (D 2)

commonly_attributed_claim: Piccinini and Bahar refute computationalism
what_the_paper_says: They defend generic computationalism and reject only its digital and analog species; neural computation is sui generis (A2 6)

commonly_attributed_claim: The Vector Grounding Problem paper shows that language models understand language
what_the_paper_says: The scope restriction is stated twice: not about understanding, knowledge, linguistic acts, or mental properties; grounding is a floor, not a ceiling (E 4)

commonly_attributed_claim: Shagrir argues that the brain is not really a computer
what_the_paper_says: He concedes that being a computer is perspectival while rescuing the empirical content of computational neuroscience; the restriction is on individuation (A2 2)

commonly_attributed_claim: Bostrom offers a fourth position on substrate independence
what_the_paper_says: He imports it as an undefended premise and states its weakest useful form; his value here is as evidence about the thesis's status in 2003 (B notes 9)

commonly_attributed_claim: Marr's computational level shows that computation is individuated non-representationally
what_the_paper_says: Three reviewed papers read Marr incompatibly: Shagrir (correspondence), Sprevak reporting Egan (function-theoretic, collapsing into representational), Piccinini & Bahar (a fallacy) (A2 notes 2)

commonly_attributed_claim: Block's 1972 and 1978 papers are two independent data points
what_the_paper_says: Block closes his own 1972 escape route in 1978 (n. 14, p. 300); the two should be presented as one developing position (A1 notes 2)

commonly_attributed_claim: The unfolding argument is a version of the philosophical zombie argument
what_the_paper_says: Section 2.5 distinguishes both scope (only causal-structure theories; it favours functionalism) and modality (a construction recipe, not a conceivability claim) (D 4)

commonly_attributed_claim: Maudlin argues against substrate independence, or that machines cannot be conscious
what_the_paper_says: He grants that silicon and hydraulic brains may be conscious (p. 429) and that computational structure may be necessary (p. 431); only sufficiency dies (F 1)

commonly_attributed_claim: Olympia is a funny-instantiation argument like Block's Chinese Nation
what_the_paper_says: He rejects those intuitions outright - 'I cannot think of one reason to accord those intuitions any weight' (p. 414); Klein separates the two families (F 2, PDF p. 8)

commonly_attributed_claim: Olympia is a triviality or exploding-implementation argument
what_the_paper_says: He presupposes, for argument's sake, that counterfactual restrictions do block explosions; the argument is best read as a dilemma (F 2, PDF p. 8)

commonly_attributed_claim: Klein refutes computationalism about consciousness
what_the_paper_says: 'I do not think Maudlin's argument succeeds' (PDF p. 7); he defends computationalism while narrowing it to architectures and actual processes (F 2)

commonly_attributed_claim: The indicator list states necessary or sufficient conditions for consciousness
what_the_paper_says: 'Systems that have more of these features are better candidates ... We do not endorse these stronger claims' (p. 45) (D 6)
